chunks: In the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful.
Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills.
And whoever associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin.

key_terms.لِمَنْ يَشَاءُ: For whom He wills (indicating divine discretion)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between major Shirk and other sins regarding divine forgiveness in Shia theology?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes this doctrine within the Shia understanding of *al-Afw* (divine pardon) versus *al-Maghfirah* (forgiveness), emphasizing that major Shirk constitutes a permanent barrier to salvation unless Allah wills otherwise, while lesser sins are subject to His discretion. This distinction underscores the Shia theological nuance that Shirk is not merely a sin but a fundamental rejection of divine sovereignty, rendering it unforgivable in its essence if one dies in that state, unlike other sins which may be excused through divine grace or intercession.
